name: Susan D. Allen
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently dated career milestone by age 26 found. BS chemistry from Colorado College in 1966 (age ~23) and PhD chemical physics from USC in 1971 (age ~28); major research and academic leadership roles came later.
early_history_summary: American engineering professor specializing in lasers and optics. Early path was conventional graduate study; professional breakthroughs and administrative leadership (Tulane, FSU, Arkansas State, Embry-Riddle) occurred well after age 26.
evidence_summary: Birth year 1943 and degree timeline (BS 1966, PhD 1971) are documented on Wikipedia and institutional profiles; no specific material professional milestone at or before age 26 is supported.

name: Kang-Xing Jin
milestone_by_age_26: After graduating Harvard CS in 2006 (same cohort as Mark Zuckerberg; HS Blair Magnet 2002 implies birth ~1984), joined Facebook as an early engineer on the News Feed team and was among the first ~30 Facebook users—material early-product engineering role at age ~22.
early_history_summary: Montgomery Blair Magnet (HS 2002) then Harvard CS (summa cum laude, Phi Beta Kappa, class of 2006). Met Zuckerberg on the first day of class; stayed to finish college while peers went to Palo Alto, then joined Facebook full-time in 2006 on News Feed and later ads engineering and product leadership.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Harvard CS cohort with Zuckerberg, early Facebook network, magnet STEM HS, News Feed engineering
evidence_summary: HS 2002 and Harvard 2006 graduation place him contemporaneous with Zuckerberg (b. 1984); Zuckerberg’s 2016 anniversary post and multiple profiles confirm he joined Facebook ~2006 as an early engineer and News Feed contributor. Birth year is inferred from cohort/HS year rather than a primary vital record, so confidence is medium. Seventeen-year Meta career culminating as Head of Health is well documented.
starting_point: Not fully documented; attended selective Montgomery Blair Magnet Program (Maryland) then Harvard CS, graduating 2006.
current_position: Former Meta VP / Head of Health (left 2023); board member Civic News Company and advisor in social-impact / digital health.

trajectory.event: Among the earliest Facebook users while at Harvard; took CS courses with Mark Zuckerberg.
Graduated Harvard CS summa cum laude and joined Facebook as an engineer on the News Feed team.
Managed Facebook ads engineering through the company’s IPO period.
Shifted toward social impact roles, later becoming Meta Head of Health.
Left Meta after ~17 years; joined civic/news and digital-health advisory boards.

name: Brett Harrison
milestone_by_age_26: Published peer-reviewed mathematics research in The American Mathematical Monthly (2007) at age ~19 after RSI at MIT; by 2010 (age 22) joined Jane Street Capital as an ADR trader and later led algorithmic trading systems development.
early_history_summary: Born in New York City, raised in Dix Hills; Half Hollow Hills HS West (2006), RSI at MIT, Harvard BA/MS in computer science (Math 55). Entered Jane Street trading/tech in 2010, later Citadel Securities technology leadership, then President of FTX US (2021–22) and founder/CEO of Architect Financial Technologies.
family_context_summary: Raised in Dix Hills, New York; detailed parental occupations and wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RSI MIT, AMM publication, Harvard CS/Math 55, Jane Street early career
evidence_summary: Birth date May 11, 1988 and 2007 AMM paper are dual-sourced (Wikipedia + JSTOR citation). Joining Jane Street in 2010 at ~22 and later leading trading-systems work is documented across Wikipedia, NYT DealBook, and BrokerCheck-linked profiles. Elite math/CS pipeline is clear; family capital not documented.
starting_point: Born in New York City and raised in Dix Hills, Long Island; selective STEM path via RSI and Harvard.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Architect Financial Technologies, a CFTC/SEC-regulated trading infrastructure and derivatives firm.

trajectory.event: Graduated high school; attended Research Science Institute at MIT as a high-school researcher.
Published mathematics research on cyclotomic polynomials in The American Mathematical Monthly.
Joined Jane Street Capital as an ADR trader and later led algorithmic trading systems groups.
Became President of FTX US, building regulated U.S. exchange operations in Chicago.
Resigned from FTX US months before the parent company’s collapse amid governance disagreements.
Founded Architect Financial Technologies with seed capital including Coinbase and Circle.

name: Bob Braden
milestone_by_age_26: No material Internet/networking milestone by age 26. Bachelor of Engineering Physics Cornell 1957 (age ~23) and MS physics Stanford 1962 (age ~28); ARPAnet/TCP/IP and UCLA IBM 360 work began around 1970 (age ~36).
early_history_summary: Physics-trained systems programmer who later attached UCLA’s IBM 360/91 to ARPAnet, contributed to FTP and TCP/IP host implementations, edited Host Requirements RFCs, and served long-term on IAB/IETF structures from ISI.
evidence_summary: Birth (1934) and death (2018) plus education and post-1970 Internet contributions are well sourced; nothing qualifies as a material milestone at or before age 26.

name: Stephen Akridge
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; cannot verify age at Intel (2006), Qualcomm (2007–2017), or Solana co-founding (~2017–2018). Without a birth year, a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established.
early_history_summary: GPU/performance engineer with multi-year Qualcomm and Intel experience who co-founded Solana Labs and contributed signature-verification GPU work; later associated with Anza and Cyber Grant Inc. Birth date not publicly documented in sources reviewed.
evidence_summary: Career timeline (Intel ~2006, long Qualcomm tenure, Solana co-founder) is available from secondary tech/legal coverage, but absence of birth year blocks age-26 eligibility under the strict rubric.

name: Meredith Broussard
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found in reviewed sources (Wikipedia omits it). Career milestones such as software work at Bell Labs/MIT Media Lab and books Artificial Unintelligence (2018) and More Than a Glitch (2023) cannot be age-dated without birth year.
early_history_summary: Data journalist and NYU professor; prior features editor at The Philadelphia Inquirer and software developer at AT&T Bell Labs and MIT Media Lab. Known for coining 'technochauvinism' and public-interest AI research.
evidence_summary: Professional profile is clear from Wikipedia and personal site, but missing birth year prevents age-at-milestone verification under strict eligibility rules.

name: Robert K. Brayton
milestone_by_age_26: No material research milestone by age 26. BSEE Iowa State 1956 (age ~22–23); PhD mathematics MIT 1961 (age ~27–28); IBM Watson career and later Berkeley logic-synthesis leadership began after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born Ames, Iowa (1933); father a high school teacher. After BSEE and ROTC/Sperry work, earned MIT PhD (1961) contributing to early LISP compiler/AI work, then 26 years at IBM Watson and long Berkeley professorship in logic synthesis and formal verification. Died 2025.
family_context_summary: Grew up in an academic environment; father was a high school teacher (Wikipedia).
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a high school teacher; not documented as an EDA/CS industry apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Birth 1933, degrees 1956/1961, and later NAE/Kanellakis-level achievements are well documented; PhD and IBM start fall after age 26, so age-26 eligibility fails.

name: J Allard
milestone_by_age_26: On January 25, 1994, at age 25, wrote the widely cited internal Microsoft memo 'Windows: The Next Killer Application on the Internet,' which helped drive Microsoft’s Internet strategy; already a program manager shipping LAN Manager/TCP-IP stack work after joining Microsoft from Boston University in 1991 (age 22).
early_history_summary: Born Glens Falls, New York (1969). Teenage BBS user; BU CS 1991; recruited into Microsoft LAN Manager/NDIS. Internet memo (1994) and TCP/IP advocacy preceded later leadership of Xbox, Xbox Live, Zune, Kin, and Courier. Later Project 529, GoFundMe CPTO, Amazon devices leadership.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace Glens Falls, NY.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early BBS/Internet use, Microsoft early-90s platform, TCP/IP wave, BU CS pipeline
evidence_summary: Birth date January 12, 1969 and 1994 memo (age 25) are corroborated by Wikipedia, NYT antitrust-era reporting, and archived memo copies. Joining Microsoft in 1991 and shipping network/Internet technologies before Xbox is dual-sourced. Family background largely undocumented.
starting_point: Born in Glens Falls, New York (1969); teenage hobbyist on computer message boards before Boston University CS.
current_position: Vice President / product leadership at Amazon (Devices & Services / ZeroOne special projects) after Microsoft, Project 529, and GoFundMe CPTO roles.

trajectory.event: Joined Microsoft from Boston University as program manager on LAN Manager / network protocols.
Authored internal memo 'Windows: The Next Killer Application on the Internet,' catalyzing Microsoft’s Internet push.
Co-founded the Xbox project, focusing on software platform, Xbox Live, and third-party ecosystem.
As CXO/CTO of Entertainment and Devices, helped launch Xbox 360 and related services.
Left Microsoft after ~19 years following Zune/Kin/Courier era product leadership.
Joined Amazon Devices and Services in a senior product/innovation role.

name: Fadi Chehadé
milestone_by_age_26: In 1987 at age ~25, founded Nett Information Products (aka Connectica), an Internet-based content management company later acquired by Ingram Micro, after BS CS (NYU Poly 1985) and MS engineering management (Stanford 1986).
early_history_summary: Born Beirut 1962 to Egyptian parents; left war-torn Lebanon in 1980 at 18. Earned CS bachelor’s (1985) and Stanford MS (1986), naturalized U.S. citizen 1986. Serial founder (Nett/Connectica, RosettaNet CEO, Viacore→IBM) and later ICANN President/CEO (2012–2016).
family_context_summary: Born in Beirut to Egyptian parents; left Lebanon amid civil war in 1980. Father helped extract him from a militia situation and send him abroad (CNN profile).
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a technology-industry family apprenticeship; Egyptian-Lebanese immigrant family context.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lebanese civil war exit, immigrant ambition, Stanford/NYU Poly, early Internet content systems
evidence_summary: Birth year 1962 and 1987 Nett founding are documented on Wikipedia and ICANN biography; AP/ICANN bios corroborate education and early entrepreneurship. Later RosettaNet and ICANN CEO roles establish broader notability. Family domain advantage is weak; adversity catalyst (war exit) is better supported.
starting_point: Born in Beirut, Lebanon (1962) to Egyptian parents; left the civil-war-torn country at 18 for the United States.
current_position: Internet entrepreneur and private-equity leader (Ethos Capital co-CEO/roles); former ICANN President and CEO (2012–2016).

trajectory.event: Earned bachelor’s degree in computer science from Polytechnic Institute of New York University.
Completed MS in engineering management at Stanford and became a naturalized U.S. citizen.
Founded Nett Information Products (Connectica), an Internet content management company later acquired by Ingram Micro.
Helped launch RosettaNet B2B standards consortium and served as its first CEO.
Appointed President and CEO of ICANN, overseeing gTLD expansion and IANA transition process.
Concluded ICANN tenure; later advised WEF and private-equity Internet investments.

evidence_summary: Wikipedia and local sports coverage establish superfan identity and software-engineer occupation but no age-26 technical milestone.

name: Brianna Wu
milestone_by_age_26: No material game-development or technology milestone by age 26. Born July 6, 1977 (CSV birth year 1987 is incorrect). Early animation studio effort around age 19 was unsuccessful; Giant Spacekat co-founded ~2010 (age ~33) and Revolution 60 released 2014 (age ~37). Fame largely tied to Gamergate-era harassment (2014) and later congressional runs.
early_history_summary: Adopted and raised in Hattiesburg, Mississippi; briefly University of Mississippi; early tech/animation experiments and political fundraising jobs. Public prominence came in the 2010s as indie game developer and activist, not by age 26.
family_context_summary: Adoptive father a retired US Navy doctor with a clinic; mother ran small businesses (Inc./depth interviews).
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents supported early tech interest with hardware and classes, but not a game-industry family business.
evidence_summary: Birth year 1977 is dual-sourced (Wikipedia, her own tweets). Material public milestones (studio, Revolution 60, Gamergate, Congress) are all after age 26.
